title: Robust optical fiber patch-cords for in vivo optogenetic experiments in rats
author: Trujillo-Pisanty, Sanio, et al.

steps.title: Review materials and plan
steps.instruction: Read the entire protocol, consult Table 1 for required items, and note that assembly takes 60–90 min. Use a 200 µm core multi‑mode fiber (0.39 NA) for a 300 µm implant, preferring a smaller core/NA than the implant to minimise light loss.

steps.title: Strip and cut fiber
steps.instruction: Use an optical‑fiber stripper to remove the buffer and expose 35 mm of cladding. Measure from the un‑stripped edge and cut the fiber to the desired length with scissors or wire cutters.

steps.title: Prepare epoxy resin
steps.instruction: Mix the heat‑curable epoxy resin according to the manufacturer’s instructions, load the mixture into a 3 mL syringe, and attach a 21‑gauge blunt‑tip needle (Braintree Scientific).

steps.title: Assemble and cure connector
steps.instruction: Place the FC (Fiber Instruments Sales) or M3 (Doric lenses) connector on a third hand with the lumen facing down. Fill the connector’s internal volume with resin, insert the fiber core completely through the connector, and cure with a heat gun until the resin darkens. Wipe off any spills before curing.

substeps.instruction: Verify a small excess drop of resin remains on the 240 µm lumen after curing; if absent, add a drop using a 26‑gauge needle or a piece of fiber buffer.

steps.title: Create groove and trim fiber
steps.instruction: Use a diamond scribe to cut a straight groove in the side of the fiber core at the edge of the hardened resin, then flick off the protruding fiber to leave a level surface without breaking the core.

substeps.instruction: If using an M3 connector, screw the internally threaded nut up to the connector.
If using an FC connector, pass the fiber through the metal boot and crimp with the appropriate tool.

steps.title: Apply shrink tubing to fiber
steps.instruction: Cut a piece of 3/64 in shrink tubing about 10 % shorter than the fiber length, slide it over the fiber until it contacts the connector, secure the fiber vertically, and heat‑shrink evenly without creating bumps.

substeps.instruction: For M3 connectors, slide the small‑bore shrink tubing (provided) over the fiber, leaving it slightly beyond the metallic end; do not shrink until polishing is complete.
For FC connectors, slide the supplied rubber protector over the metallic boot.

steps.title: Thread spring and strip segment
steps.instruction: Pass the fiber through the stainless‑steel compression spring, then strip 45–50 mm of fiber beyond the connector, leaving a gap of 5–8 mm (acceptable) between the shrink tubing and the exposed cladding.

steps.title: Insert fiber into ferrule
steps.instruction: Place a stainless‑steel ferrule (240 µm drilled side down) in a third hand, fill its interior with heat‑curable epoxy, and feed the exposed fiber core through until it cannot advance further. Remove all resin from the fiber core with a delicate‑task wipe and alcohol, then heat‑cure the epoxy, leaving ~40 mm of fiber protruding from the ferrule.

steps.title: Attach second ferrule and cure
steps.instruction: Fasten a ceramic split sleeve to a second ferrule so that the 240 µm lumen faces away and about one‑quarter of the ferrule remains exposed. Load this ferrule with epoxy, allow resin to enter the sleeve, insert the fiber core through until both ferrules contact inside the sleeve, remove excess resin, and heat‑cure. Ensure a small excess of resin remains at the ferrule tip; if not, add a tiny drop. Use the diamond scribe to make a groove at the resin edge and flick‑cut the fiber at the groove level.

steps.title: Add spring and adhesive tubing
steps.instruction: Push the compression spring over the fiber until it contacts the ferrule, then insert the ferrule‑assembly into a 2 in piece of adhesive shrink tubing. Advance the ferrules until the tip protrudes and the tubing covers the spring and most of the ceramic sleeve. Heat‑shrink, applying light pressure while hot to ensure tight contact; avoid adhesive spilling onto the exposed ferrule.

steps.title: Heat‑shrink tip reinforcement
steps.instruction: Slide the stiffened tip into a ~2 in length of 1/4 in shrink tubing and heat‑shrink. Repeat with additional layers as needed (minimum one layer) to achieve the desired rigidity and external diameter, leaving the ferrule exposed.

steps.title: Polish fiber tip
steps.instruction: Polish the tip on 5 µm silicon‑carbide paper using a figure‑eight pattern on a polishing puck; keep the ferrule vertical and avoid excessive pressure. Clean with isopropyl alcohol and a delicate‑task wipe. Repeat on 3 µm, then 1 µm, then 0.3 µm papers, lubricating with a drop of distilled water between grits, until the fiber core appears circular, light‑gray, smooth, and scratch‑free under a 200× fiber scope. Polish the opposite (FC) connector similarly. For M3 connectors, clamp a straight hemostat to the tip, keep it flat against the paper, and follow the same progressive‑grit sequence.

steps.title: Test optical performance
steps.instruction: Connect the patch‑cord to the optical rotary joint (or light source) in the behavioral apparatus. Point the tip at a vertical non‑reflective surface, turn on the light source at low power (wear protective goggles), and verify a pattern of concentric rings. Measure output with a photodiode sensor and optical‑power meter, adjust laser power, and confirm that loss per connection is ≤15 % and that the cord transmits at least 10 % more power than required for the experiment.

steps.title: Insert metal ferrule into sleeve
steps.instruction: Insert the metal ferrule attached to the animal’s implant halfway into a ceramic sleeve so that it contacts the patch‑cord ferrule inside the sleeve.

steps.title: Record final dimensions
steps.instruction: Measure and note that the completed patch‑cord is 2.32 ft (71 cm) long and weighs approximately 0.49 oz (14 g).
